2F.9 Adhere to God's will, for He will try and prove you to see whether or not you will walk in His law and keep His commandments.
2G.6 Do not covenant with the heathen or their gods, or keep company with the heathen and idolaters.
3G.4 We are not to consent with sinners and evildoers, or walk with them, or sit down with them.
4C.2 Bribery condemned as being wicked and perverting justice and judgment.

precepts.text: Although I have cast them far off among the heathen and scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.
precepts.point: A lot of us do not like going to the Sabbath, do not like congregating, hear the class and they are out. We have to love the habitation of His house; these are the things that continually build us up.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
“Lord, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.” David is talking about Jerusalem, but we also have little sanctuaries: “Therefore say, Thus saith the Lord God; Although I have cast them far off among the heathen, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet will I be to them as a little sanctuary in the countries where they shall come.”

Though He cast us far off among the heathen and scattered us among the countries, He is to us a little sanctuary in the countries where we come. Those are the little congregations in Florida, Georgia, New York, Uganda, France, Russia.

Honor is the keeping of the commandments of God, the love between a husband and wife, making marriages great again. David loved everything that came with keeping the commandments: congregating, seeing your brothers and sisters, going for counsel, getting corrected. A lot of us do not like going to the Sabbath, do not like congregating, hear the class and they are out. We have to love the habitation of His house, because these are the things that continually build us up.

precepts.text: The gifts are given for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ, till we all come into the unity of the faith unto a perfect man.
precepts.point: When he is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
“My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the Lord.” The congregations are where the gifts are at work: “For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ”.

The gifts are given for the perfecting of the saints, the work of the ministry and the edifying of the body of Christ, till we all come into the unity of the faith unto a perfect man. That is what keeps the foot standing in an even place, stable and steadfast in the truth.

When David is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

precepts.text: That we henceforth be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men and cunning craftiness whereby they lie in wait to deceive.
precepts.point: When he is able to congregate and be among his people, he blesses the Lord by keeping His laws, keeping His statutes, and going out declaring His glory to the children of Israel, showing them who they are, where they come from, and where they are going.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

precepts.why:
His foot standing in an even place means he is stable and steadfast in his truth, not tossed to and fro: “That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive”.

There is no sleight of hand happening to him, no wind of doctrine throwing him around. The sleight of hand and cunning craftiness is the deception hitting our brothers and sisters: the sunrise sabbath, "you can eat whatever you want to." God is not about that. The foot stands even in the congregations, where the body of Christ is edified and not carried about.

Still on Revelation 16:15: he will come upon you like a thief; watch and have your garments on. David said, “Examine me, O Lord, and prove me; try my reins and my heart.” Test me. That is why Sirach said when you come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation. God proves us according to our own lusts and desires, and these tests decide whether we win or lose. Either you win or you learn: lose means you left; learn means I fell, I’m getting back up, Lord, I’m staying in this truth and enduring to the end.

points: Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in mine integrity; I have trusted also in the Lord, therefore I shall not slide. We slide back into the world when we do not trust the Most High.

The employer asks you to work this Saturday. Are you going to keep the laws even when you know you need the money? Will you make the shekel great and the ephah small, or make the ephah, the laws of the Lord, great and the shekel small? Trust that the Lord is going to make a way.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: Examine me, O Lord, and prove me; try my reins and my heart.

When we examine ourselves we forget to ask the Lord to examine us. Lord, show me the things that are not right in me, especially going into a proving process or about to get married: show me what baggage I still have so I do not go into it with extra luggage.
You are on Spirit Airlines trying to carry all this luggage to new heights, new levels, new destinations; guess what, you are going to pay for it, it is going to hit you if you are not ready.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes and I have walked in thy truth. I have not sat with vain persons, neither will I go in with dissemblers.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: David did not hang around haters, complainers, or people always talking about other people. He did not hang around those complaining "this unleavened bread is not good, this Sabbath food is not good." He did not sit with vain persons who have no value to you in this truth, whether at the job, the gym, or even family members.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: I have hated the congregation of evildoers and will not sit with the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: I will wash mine hands in innocency, so will I compass thine altar, O Lord, that I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving and tell of all thy wondrous works.

Washing your hands in innocency means you have nothing to do with it. A brother comes and says "she looking right, you think I should talk to her?" and you say, "I think you should keep the commandments, are you going to marry her?"

note.label: Psalm 26: I Have Walked in Mine Integrity

points: But as for me, I will walk in mine integrity; redeem me and be merciful unto me.
